earlier_conventions.observation: Perfect means locally represented by a bounded complex of finite free modules, with arbitrary integer endpoints. I4.11 explicitly sends amplitude[a,b] to[a−n,b−n] under the shift[n]. Thus k[2], with its only term in degree−2, satisfies the actual perfectness convention.

The group uses the full category D(X)_uparf; no cohomological nonnegativity is imposed. IV1.2(a) explicitly records cl(L[n])=(−1)^n cl(L). The triangle L→0→L[1]→L[1] gives cl(L[1])=−cl(L), and iteration gives the displayed shift rule.

earlier_conventions.observation: VI2 identifies the K group with the perfect-complex group and uses D-plus, which permits any finite lower bound. Its mention of O(1) in degree0 defines the generator, without restricting arbitrary perfect complexes. The introduction to VI6 explicitly recalls the comparison with the locally-free group via IV2.9. Definition6.5 then quantifies over a perfect M-bullet(Y) with no additional degree condition.

earlier_conventions.source: VI365–410 text search and inspected definition passages
earlier_conventions.observation: The references to positive graded algebras and homogeneous module components in VI1–2 are attached to those explicitly graded algebra/module constructions. No located text transfers a nonnegative cohomological restriction to the arbitrary perfect M-bullet(Y) of6.5. The explicit shift convention above already supplies its negative-degree examples.

projection_between_the_two_sums.map: The all-degree sum H_all(M)=direct-sum over i∈Z of H^i(M) has the canonical projection to H_ge0(M)=direct-sum over i≥0. It is identity on each nonnegative-degree summand and zero on each negative-degree summand.
projection_between_the_two_sums.kernel: Its kernel is exactly the direct sum over i<0. The canonical inclusion of nonnegative summands splits the projection. No identification of these two sums is asserted for a general M.

counterexample_to_6_6.data: X=Spec k, d=0, L=O_X and M=k[2], the one-term finite free complex in degree−2.
counterexample_to_6_6.class: The distinguished-triangle shift relation gives cl(M)=cl(k)=1. This class is nonzero: the finite Euler dimension sum on bounded finite-dimensional complexes is additive on distinguished triangles, by the associated finite long exact cohomology sequence, and sends cl(k) to1∈Z.
counterexample_to_6_6.support: All H^i(M) with i≥0 vanish. The printed H-star therefore has empty support, satisfying the positive codimension condition for every closed Y of the point. The printed6.5 places1 in K^bullet(X)_1, whereas6.6 with d=0 claims that group is zero.
counterexample_to_6_6.failed_inference: The sentence on412 uses empty support of H-star to conclude M acyclic. The concrete M above is not acyclic: H^(−2)(M)=k.

counterexample_to_printed_tensor_support.data: On Spec k take M=k[−2], whose cohomology is in degree2, and N=k[2], whose cohomology is in degree−2.
counterexample_to_printed_tensor_support.map: The total tensor is the one-term complex k⊗_k k in degree0; multiplication a⊗b↦ab identifies it with k, with inverse c↦c⊗1. Both shifts are even, so the differential signs do not alter this explicit identification.
counterexample_to_printed_tensor_support.failure: Its printed nonnegative cohomology has support X, but the printed nonnegative cohomology of N has empty support. Thus the very support inclusion used at the top of412 also fails with the printed index.

all_degree_support_in_the_actual_proof.acyclicity: Empty support of the sum over every integer means every cohomology sheaf is zero, exactly the definition that M is acyclic; its distinguished-triangle Grothendieck class is then0.
all_degree_support_in_the_actual_proof.tensor_support: At a point outside total cohomology support of M, the stalk complex M_x is acyclic. A bounded free representative splits into two-term contractible summands by splitting the last surjection and descending through its finite degrees. Its contracting homotopy h gives the contracting homotopy h⊗id on the total tensor with a bounded free representative of N_x; the two mixed differential terms cancel by the usual total-complex signs. Hence the tensor stalk is acyclic. The same argument applies with M and N exchanged, giving exactly the intersection-support inclusion printed on412.

why_the_index_edit_is_determined.argument: Every integer q occurs as the sole cohomological degree of the actual allowed perfect complex k[−q]. Omitting q from a fixed summation index set makes that sum zero for k[−q], while its class(−1)^q remains nonzero. Therefore no omitted integer is compatible with the source’s unrestricted-perfect-complex acyclicity step and6.6. Including all integers is the forced index set when the repair is confined to this index and the remainder of6.5–6.6 is preserved.
why_the_index_edit_is_determined.editorial_scope: This identifies a minimal supported repair, not an unseen author-draft intention. Restricting the class of representatives would be a larger textual change; the equivalence below explains that alternative without inserting it into the source.

even_shift_comparison_with_nonnegative_r.boundedness: For the noetherian X in6.5, quasi-compactness and a finite cover by bounded finite-free local representatives give a global lower and upper bound[a,b] for the cohomology of each perfect M.
even_shift_comparison_with_nonnegative_r.shift: Choose an integer N≥0 with a+2N≥0 and apply the exact shift[−2N]. Its inverse is[2N]. The identity H^i(M[−2N])=H^(i−2N)(M) identifies each cohomology sheaf with the reindexed old one, so their all-degree supports coincide. The shift lemma gives cl(M[−2N])=cl(M).
even_shift_comparison_with_nonnegative_r.filtration: For every closed Y, this sends a representative for the repaired all-degree condition to a nonnegative-cohomology representative with the same class and support. Conversely, every representative with vanishing negative cohomology has identical all-degree and nonnegative sums. Thus the explicitly restricted-representative filtration coincides with the repaired all-degree filtration, through these exact shifts; the unrestricted printed definition does not impose that restriction.

conclusion: Recommend current-only replacement of the cohomological index i≥0 by i∈Z in6.5, retaining the printed index diplomatically. Preserve every other hypothesis, class map and support formula. The immediate source proof and explicit allowed shifts determine this local repair.
